extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and practitioners filing U.S. nonprovisional utility and plant patent applications seeking prioritized (Track One) examination
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for requesting prioritized (Track One) examination at the USPTO, including eligibility, filing items and methods, fees, RCE-specific rules, events that terminate status, and refund/appeal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of prioritized examination (Track One)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritized examination is a procedure for expedited examination of a patent application under 37 CFR 1.102(e). Prioritized examination of new applications is also known as the Track One program. A request for prioritized examination may also be filed with or after a request for continued examination (RCE) but before the mailing of the first Office action subsequent to the RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the governing regulation (37 CFR 1.102(e)) and the permitted timing relative to RCEs (filed with or after an RCE but before the first Office action after the RCE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Original nonprovisional utility and plant patent applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) are eligible for Track One.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'original application' includes first filings and continuing applications (continuation, continuation-in-part, divisional). Reissue applications are not eligible. Continuing applications are not automatically given Track One status based on a request filed in the parent application; each application must meet requirements and have a timely request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim limits for eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time the request is reviewed by the Office of Petitions, the application must have no more than four independent claims, thirty total claims, and no multiple dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These claim limits are strictly applied when reviewing the request for participation; exceeding them can lead to dismissal or denial of the Track One request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date eligibility constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be filed on or after September 26, 2011 to be eligible for the Track One program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program applies only to applications filed on/after the effective date noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual cap on granted requests (20,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a limit of 20,000 granted requests for prioritized examination for the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 20,000 limit applies to the sum of all granted requests for prioritized examination, including both Track One and prioritized examination for RCEs. For 37 CFR 1.102(e), 'accept' means 'grant'. Track One filing rate information is available via the USPTO Track One Data dashboard.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit a Track One request (filing method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for Prioritized Examination of utility patent applications must be filed electronically via the Patent Electronic System (EFS-Web, Patent Center). Requests for plant applications may be filed in paper or electronically as provided for in the May 2020 Official Notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Request for Prioritized Examination must be present on filing of the original utility or plant application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), or with or after an RCE in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114. A quick start guide and Patent Electronic Business Center contact info are provided for electronic filing questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PTO/AIA/424 form
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of PTO/AIA/424 is not required, but applicants are encouraged to use this form to avoid processing delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using your own form, it should include the same certification and request information as PTO/AIA/424. If your form is a modified version of PTO/AIA/424, remove any text identifying it as an Office form and do not modify certification language. See 37 CFR 1.4(d)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees required with Request for Prioritized Examination (original application)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following fees must be paid for a Request for Prioritized Examination for a new application: prioritized examination fee (37 CFR 1.17(c)); prioritized examination processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)(1)); basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(a) or plant 1.16(c)); search fee (37 CFR 1.16(k) or plant 1.16(m)); examination fee (37 CFR 1.16(o) or plant 1.16(q)); excess claim fee (37 CFR 1.16(h) and (i)); application size fee (37 CFR 1.16(s)); publication fee (37 CFR 1.18(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publication fee is currently set to $0 but remains a requirement in case it changes. If required excess claim or application size fees are unpaid at the time the request is considered, applicant will be notified and must pay within one month of a first decision on the request. If any of fees (i)-(v) and (viii) are unpaid at time of filing, the request will be dismissed unless an explicit authorization to charge missing fees is provided in the papers. Applicants are encouraged to include authorization to charge additional fees under 37 CFR 1.16 and 1.17. Refer to the current fee schedule for exact amounts and entity discounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items that must be present upon filing
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered for Track One, the application must include upon filing: a Request for Prioritized Examination; a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 including at least one claim; any required drawings; either an executed inventor's oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63/1.64 for each inventor, or a signed ADS that provides each inventor's legal name, mailing address, and residence (if different); and the required fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All these items must be present on filing (or effectively present via same-day follow-on submission) to meet the 'present upon filing' requirement of 37 CFR 1.102(e)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility with foreign priority or provisional benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: An original utility or plant nonprovisional application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) and claiming priority to a foreign application under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) or (f), or claiming benefit of a U.S. provisional application, is eligible for Track One.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such priority/benefit claims do not disqualify eligibility; instructions for translations or other requirements may apply in particular cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: International application / national stage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for prioritized examination may be made in a U.S. application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) which claims the benefit of an earlier international application under 35 U.S.C. 365(c) (bypass continuation) or claims priority/right of priority under 365(a), subject to conditions of 35 U.S.C. 365. However, an applicant may not request prioritized examination of a national stage application filed under 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the earlier international application was not filed in English and the filing is a bypass continuation, a translation is required in accordance with 37 CFR 1.52(b)(1)(ii). See questions 15 and 18 for related RCE/national-stage info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statements and inventor oath exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a joint inventor refuses to execute an oath or declaration and a substitute statement is prepared, the substitute statement and other inventor declarations or a properly signed ADS must be submitted on the date the application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.64 for details on substitute statements and USPTO examples ('Inventor’s Oath or Declaration Examples') for best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublication requests with Track One
rubrics_metrics.description: You may file an application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) with both a nonpublication request and a Track One request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publication fee (37 CFR 1.18(d)) must still be submitted to comply with prioritized examination requirements (currently set to $0). Check the current fee schedule for amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: When prioritized examination can be requested with an RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: You may file a prioritized examination request with an RCE under 37 CFR 1.102(e)(2) if: the application is an original nonprovisional utility/plant filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or has entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371; and a proper RCE is filed concurrently with the prioritized examination request OR an RCE was filed previously but an Office action responsive to that RCE has not yet been mailed; and no previous prioritized examination request for an RCE has been granted in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, the application must contain (or be amended to contain) no more than four independent claims, thirty total claims, and no multiple dependent claims. A proper RCE requires that prosecution in the application be closed (e.g., last Office action is final, a notice of allowance, or otherwise closes prosecution). See 37 CFR 1.114(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees required when filing with an RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: To request prioritized examination with an RCE, the following fees must be paid in addition to any RCE fees: prioritized examination fee (37 CFR 1.17(c)); prioritized examination processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)(1)); if not previously paid, the publication fee (37 CFR 1.18(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since the publication fee is currently $0, no publication fee is due at this time for an RCE. If any required fees are unpaid when filed, the prioritized examination request will be dismissed unless explicit authorization to charge additional fees is provided in the papers. Applicants are encouraged to include authorization to charge additional fees under 37 CFR 1.16 and 1.17. See current fee schedule for exact amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability for national stage via RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon filing a proper RCE (which requires prosecution to be closed), prioritized examination becomes available for an application filed as a national stage entry under 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows national-stage applications to use Track One only via the proper RCE mechanism, not at initial 371 filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single RCE prioritization limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The prioritized examination program permits a single request to be granted upon filing a new application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), and a single request to be granted upon filing an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 in that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prioritized examination has already been granted for an RCE in the application, another prioritized request with a later RCE will not be granted. If prioritized examination was granted at original filing, you may still file a request with an RCE provided prioritized examination has not previously been granted for an RCE in that application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events that terminate or suspend Track One special status
rubrics_metrics.description: Track One special status remains until one of the following occurs: applicant files a petition for extension of time for filing a reply; applicant files an amendment that causes the application to contain >4 independent claims, >30 total claims, or a multiple dependent claim; applicant files an RCE; applicant files a notice of appeal; applicant files a request for suspension of action; a notice of allowance is mailed; a final Office action is mailed; the application is abandoned; or examination is completed as defined in 37 CFR 41.102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any of these events will terminate special status; specific procedural effects and MPEP references apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO time goal for final disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's goal is to provide a final disposition within twelve months, on average, from the date that Track One status was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a program target (goal), not a guaranteed statutory deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementing omitted items same day
rubrics_metrics.description: If an item was inadvertently omitted from the initial electronic filing, you may supply the missing item via a follow-on submission on the same day so that all necessary items are effectively 'present upon filing'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only registered users of the Patent Electronic System can submit follow-on documents via the System. Example: filing fees omitted can be submitted as a same-day follow-on submission. See MPEP 502.05(I)(C)(5) for examples of implications of omitted items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-examination notices delay decision (but not dismissal)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-examination notice identifying missing items or informalities will delay a decision on a Track One request until applicant files a complete and timely reply to the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common causes: papers not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52, missing English-language specification, missing excess claims fees. Pre-examination notices generally define a period for reply. Any request for an extension of time to reply to such a notice will cause the application to be ineligible for further Track One treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of preliminary amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment filed in an application that included a Track One request will not result in dismissal of the request, or termination of special status if already granted, so long as the preliminary amendment does not cause the application to contain more than four independent claims, more than thirty total claims, or a multiple dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that do not violate claim limits are tolerated and will not negate Track One status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing an Information Disclosure Statement (IDS)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed in an application that includes a Track One request will not result in dismissal of a pending request, or termination of special status if a request has already been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also 37 CFR 1.97; IDS filings are allowed during Track One prosecution without adverse automatic effects on status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of petitions for extension or requests for suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If you petition for an extension of time to reply or request suspension of action when a Track One request is pending, the request will be dismissed. If the Track One request was already granted, such a petition or request will terminate the application's Track One status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if Track One status is terminated by such a petition/request, the petition/request itself will still be acted upon as set forth in MPEP 708.02(b)(II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of dismissal (petition under 37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe a decision dismissing your request for prioritized examination is not proper, you may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the specific reasons for dismissal in the decision before filing a petition. If the prioritized examination request was filed at the time of an RCE, you may alternatively file a new Request for Prioritized Examination (must include proper fees and be timely—filed prior to mailing of the first Office action after the RCE). The Office of Petitions can assist with questions regarding specific decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee refunds after dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Track One request is dismissed, the prioritized examination fee (37 CFR 1.17(c)) will be automatically refunded; the prioritized examination processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)(1)) will be retained to cover processing costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the publication fee is set to an amount other than $0, you may request a refund of the publication fee under MPEP 1126 if the application is not published. For a dismissed Track One request filed with an original application, you may request a refund of the search fee and any excess claims fees by filing a petition for express abandonment (form PTO/AIA/24B) before an examination has been made; basic filing fee, examination fee, and required application size fee cannot be refunded. Refund requests for search/excess fees must be concurrent with or within two months of the declaration of express abandonment; see MPEP 711.01(III).
